questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 5]

A botanist is conducting an experiment which studies the growth of plants. The heights of the plants are measured on seven different days.

Number of days (d)   | 2 | 5 | 13 | 24 | 33 | 37 | 42
Average height (h cm)| 10| 16| 30 | 59 | 76 | 79 | 82

(a) The regression line of h on d for this data can be written in the form h = ad + b. Find a and b. [2]

(b) Write down the value of Pearson’s product-moment correlation coefficient, r. [1]

(c) Use your regression line to estimate the average height of the plants when the experiment has been running for 20 days. [2]
questions.summary: Calculate and use a linear regression and correlation coefficient.

2. [Maximum mark: 6]

The following diagram shows two buildings situated on level ground. From point P on the ground directly between the two buildings, the angle of elevation to the top of each building is θ.

[Diagram not to scale: PA=150 m to the top A of the taller building; PB=90 m to top B of the shorter; AB=154 m. The equal elevation angles at P are θ, and the taller height is h.]

(a) Find the measure of APB̂. [3]

(b) Find the height, h, of the taller building. [3]

3. [Maximum mark: 5]

The amount of a drug, in milligrams (mg), in a patient’s body can be modelled by A(t) = 500e^(−kt), where k is a positive constant and t is the time in hours after the initial dose is given.

(a) Write down the amount of the drug in the patient’s body when t = 0. [1]

After three hours, the amount has decreased to 280 mg.

(b) Find k. [2]

The second dose is given T hours after the initial dose, when the amount is 140 mg.

(c) Find T. [2]
questions.summary: Determine parameters and times in an exponential decay model.

4. [Maximum mark: 8]

The weights, W grams, of bags of rice packaged in a factory can be modelled by a normal distribution with mean 204 grams and standard deviation 5 grams.

(a) Find P(W > 210). [2]

According to this model, 80% of the bags weigh between w grams and 210 grams.

(b) Find P(W < w). [2]

(c) Find w. [2]

(d) Ten bags are selected at random. Find the probability that exactly one weighs less than w grams. [2]
questions.summary: Apply normal and binomial distributions to bag weights.

questions.accessible_text:
5. [Maximum mark: 7]

The expansion of (x + h)⁸, where h > 0, can be written as x⁸ + ax⁷ + bx⁶ + cx⁵ + dx⁴ + … + h⁸, where a, b, c, d, … ∈ ℝ.

(a) Find an expression, in terms of h, for (i) a; (ii) b; (iii) d. [4]

(b) Given that a, b and d are the first three terms of a geometric sequence, find h. [3]
questions.summary: Use the binomial theorem and a geometric-sequence condition.
questions.solution: (a) From the binomial expansion, a=8h, b=28h² and d=70h⁴. (b) For consecutive geometric terms, b²=ad. Thus (28h²)²=(8h)(70h⁴), giving 784h⁴=560h⁵. Since h>0, h=784/560=1.4.

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 6]

A particle moves in a straight line such that its velocity, v m s⁻¹, at time t seconds is given by v(t) = 4e^(−t/3)cos(t/2 − π/4), for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4π.

[Graph: v starts positive, rises slightly to a first maximum, crosses the t-axis, reaches a negative minimum and approaches zero from below by t=4π.]

Let t₁ be the first time when the particle’s acceleration is zero.

(a) Find t₁. [2]

Let t₂ be the second time when the particle is instantaneously at rest.

(b) Find t₂. [2]

(c) Find the distance travelled between t=t₁ and t=t₂. [2]
questions.summary: Use numerical differentiation, roots and integration for damped oscillatory motion.
questions.solution: (a) Solve v′(t)=0; the first solution is t₁=arctan(5/12)=0.394791…≈0.395 s. (b) v=0 when cos(t/2−π/4)=0. The second such time is t₂=7π/2=10.9956…≈11.0 s. (c) Accounting for the sign change at 3π/2, distance = ∫_(t₁)^(3π/2)v(t)dt − ∫_(3π/2)^(7π/2)v(t)dt =7.83118…≈7.83 m.

questions.accessible_text:
7. [Maximum mark: 15]

Consider the function h(x) = √(4x − 2), for x ≥ 1/2.

(a) (i) Find h⁻¹(x), the inverse of h(x), and state its domain.
    (ii) Write down the range of h⁻¹(x). [5]

(b) The graph of h intersects the graph of h⁻¹ at two points. Find the x-coordinates of these two points. [3]

(c) Find the area enclosed by the graph of h and the graph of h⁻¹. [2]

(d) Find h′(x). [2]

(e) Find the value of x for which the graph of h and the graph of h⁻¹ have the same gradient. [3]
questions.summary: Find an inverse, intersections, enclosed area and equal-gradient point.
questions.solution: (a)(i) y=√(4x−2) gives x=(y²+2)/4, so h⁻¹(x)=(x²+2)/4 with domain x≥0. (ii) Its range is y≥1/2. (b) Intersections lie on y=x: √(4x−2)=x, giving x²−4x+2=0, so x=2±√2. (c) ∫_(2−√2)^(2+√2)[h(x)−h⁻¹(x)]dx=1.88561…≈1.89. (d) h′(x)=2/√(4x−2). (e) Equate 2/√(4x−2) to x/2; numerical solution in the domain is x=1.772776…≈1.77.

8. [Maximum mark: 13]

A weight suspended on a spring is pulled down and released, so that it moves up and down vertically. The height, H metres, of the base of the weight above the ground can be modelled by H(t) = a cos(7.8t) + b, for a, b ∈ ℝ and 0 ≤ t ≤ 10, where t is seconds after release.

[Diagram: a weight suspended from a spring above the ground.]

(a) Find the period. [2]

The weight is released at a minimum height of 1 m and reaches a maximum of 1.8 m.

[Graph: H oscillates between 1 and 1.8 over 0≤t≤10, starting at H=1.]

(b) Find (i) a; (ii) b. [3]

(c) Find the number of times the weight reaches its maximum height in the first five seconds. [2]

(d) Find the first time the base reaches 1.5 m. [2]

A camera takes a picture at a random time during the first five seconds.

(e) Find the probability that the height is greater than 1.5 m. [4]
questions.summary: Analyse a sinusoidal spring-height model and a time-based probability.
questions.solution: (a) Period=2π/7.8=10π/39≈0.806 s. (b) The midline is (1.8+1)/2=1.4, and because H(0) is the minimum, a=−0.4 and b=1.4. (c) Maxima occur at about 0.403,1.21,2.01,2.82,3.62,4.43: 6 times. (d) Solve −0.4cos(7.8t)+1.4=1.5; the first time is 0.233779…≈0.234 s. (e) Within each period H>1.5 from t=0.233779… to 0.571757…, lasting 0.337978…. Six such intervals occur in five seconds, so probability=6(0.337978…)/5=0.405574…≈0.406.

9. [Maximum mark: 15]

A bag contains n balls. Ten are green and the rest red. Balls are drawn one after another without replacement.

(a) Find, in terms of n, the probability that (i) the first ball is green; (ii) the first two balls are green. [3]

For the following parts let n=25.

(b) Show that the probability the first two balls are red is 0.35. [2]

(c) Find the probability the first three balls are all red. [2]

(d) Find the probability at least one of the first three balls is green. [2]

A game draws four balls without replacement, then replaces all four. A player earns zero points if no green is picked, or if the first green is on draw 1 or 2; 10 points if the first green is on draw 3; and 50 points if the first green is on draw 4. Millie plays k games and adds her points.

(e) Find the least k such that Millie’s expected score is greater than 100. [6]
questions.summary: Apply without-replacement probabilities and expected value to a repeated game.
